Fact checks›Budget & spending

The claim

A councilman said the city has no money

“Brett Wright talked about how broke the city is and how there is NO MONEY.”

Seen: Eagle Mountain City Tax Referendum Facebook group, August 2026. First seen August 21, 2026.

Our finding Unsupported by the record

The record is complete enough to check it, and does not bear it out.

Not what the recording has him saying. His argument that night was about choices and about not standing for re-election, not about an empty account.

The numbers

Wright's stated positionseconded the rate motion, then said he will not run againVoted yes
Transportation plan, city shareby 2035, per Councilmember Wood$419,000,000

What’s true

Wright did speak at length about the city's finances at the August 6 hearing, and the council as a body did argue that the current revenue mix is not holding. He seconded the motion that set the rate.

Where it goes wrong

What he actually said was that the easy path would have been to do nothing and keep cutting services, and that he is in his fifth year and will not run again. His stated reason for voting without an electoral calculation in it. The council's case was structural rather than “no money”: sales tax is being consumed by the sheriff's contract, leaving intersections without signals; sales tax collapses in a downturn and the need for police does not; and Councilmember Wood put the city's share of the master transportation plan at $419 million by 2035. Residents in the same room argued the opposite, that the city already has the money.

More detail

The transcript of this meeting is now speaker-attributed, so the remarks above can be read against his name rather than inferred. The chair hands off to each member by name before they speak (“Okay, thank you. Councilmember Wright, go ahead”), and Wright's reply runs from there to “My time's about out, but thank you for being here.” Nothing in it says the city has no money.

The later open deliberation is a different matter: after about 03:42 members interrupt each other and the chair stops introducing anyone, so that stretch is left unattributed on the site rather than guessed. The second quotation below sits in that stretch, which is why it is credited to a councilmember and not to a named one.
